findings.title: Every success criterion traces to at least one task
findings.description:
Cross-referencing the slice design's Success Criteria against the tasks:

- **Functional requirements:** PASS-per-file and exit 0 → Task 4 + Task 4T real-design tests + Task 5 walkthrough step 1. FAIL with `missing:` lines and exit 1 → Task 4 output bullets, Task 4T broken-copy test, Task 5 step 2. Doctype failure → Task 3 (per-file `reason: 'doctype'`), Task 3T (quoted and missing `docType`), Task 4T, Task 5 step 3. Multi-file in-order with later files still checked → Task 3, Task 3T, Task 4T. All exit-2 triggers (no args, missing/non-regular file, template errors, empty stdout in both modes, valid-before-missing ordering, `cf guides update` message) → Task 3 preflight bullet (line 77), Task 3T errors bullet (line 91), Task 4 exit-2 bullet, Task 4T exit-2-with-empty-stdout tests, Task 5 step 4. `--json` contract with `template` absolute and `reason` only-when-set → Task 4 and Task 4T. Worktree-own-guide template → Task 4 resolution bullets and Task 4T's worktree-aware template test.
- **Technical requirements:** all four unit-test categories (normalization cases, level mismatch, fenced-block ignore, CRLF) → Task 2T; real-template file-level test asserting non-empty required list including `## Overview` and `### Verification Walkthrough` → Task 3T; real-slice-designs command test including the 214 document → Task 4T; build/lint/full-suite and ~300-line limits → per-task success criteria plus Task 6. I verified the named anchors exist: `GUIDE_RELATIVE_PATH` at `packages/core/src/guides/types.ts:313`, the template with `<!-- required -->` markers at `project-documents/ai-project-guide/project-guides/templates/slice-design.md`, the bash parity script in `project-documents/ai-project-guide/scripts/`, `parseFrontmatter`, the pure/file split (`frontmatterSchema.js` in `index.ts`, `frontmatterFileValidator.js` in `node.ts`), `withJsonOption`/`withProjectOption` (`packages/cli/src/options.ts`), `handleError` (`packages/cli/src/utils/errors.ts`), and both cited test-pattern files in `packages/cli/tests/commands/`.
- **Integration requirement** (guide repoints references and removes the script) is explicitly guide-session work per the design's Excluded list; the cf-side enabler is the output-contract parity Task 5 verifies, and the post-release handoff is correctly noted in the Context Summary as not a task here.

findings.title: Sequencing, granularity, and commit placement are sound
findings.description: Ordering is dependency-correct with no cycles: branch (Task 0) → constant (Task 1) → pure validator → its tests → commit → file layer → its tests → commit → subcommand → its tests → commit → walkthrough/parity → docs/full validation. Each test task immediately follows its implementation (2→2T, 3→3T, 4→4T), and commit markers sit at working, tested points after each implementation+test pair, with conditional commits only for the tasks that may not change files (Task 5C, 6C) — Task 1's change rides into the 2C commit, which is an acceptable working point. Effort sizes (1–3) match the content; no task needs splitting and none is so granular it should merge (Task 0 is the standard branch gate). Test volume matches exactly what the design's Technical Requirements enumerate — no surplus test tasks. No NFRs appear in the slice, so no `tests/load/` or CI-gating task is owed. I verified no scope creep: Task 2T's `#hashtag` case traces to the design's heading-regex decision, Task 3T's quoted-`docType` case traces to the leniency decision, and the breakdown keeps all four design exclusions (no `cf check` wiring, no guide edits, no content checks, no env override) out of the tasks.

findings.title: The "unreadable file" preflight branch is implemented but never exercised by any test
findings.description: The slice's functional requirement lists "a missing, non-regular or unreadable file" among the exit-2 triggers, and Task 3's preflight bullet implements all three checks. Task 3T's error list covers missing (valid-file-then-missing), non-regular (directory passed as file), and both template error cases — but no task tests an existing-but-unreadable file, so that preflight branch ships unverified. The design's own Technical Requirements don't enumerate an unreadable-file test and the walkthrough doesn't exercise it, so this is a minor gap, not a blocker: adding one line to Task 3T's errors bullet (e.g., a file with permissions stripped, guarded for root-running environments) would close it.
